According to the 2020 Pew Research, 25% of the Turks said homosexuality should be accepted by society, with 57% opposing it. The acceptance was higher among educated people (41%) and youth (34%).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pewresearch.org/global/2020/06/25/global-divide-on-homosexuality-persists/|title=The Global Divide on Homosexuality Persists|newspaper=Pew Research Center|date=25 June 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref>

==Living conditions==
Homosexuality is a taboo subject in Turkey{{Citation needed|date=September 2026|reason=needs recent cite}} and the culture of "[[honour killing]]s" can be observed in some families murdering members (usually female) who engage in sexual behaviours regarded by some as morally inappropriate. The [[murder of Ahmet Yıldız]], a 26-year-old Kurdish gay man from [[Urfa|Şanlıurfa]], may be the first known example of an honour killing with a gay male victim.<ref name="taz.de"/><ref name="report with details on the killing"/><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/was-ahmet-yildiz-the-victim-of-turkeys-first-gay-honour-killing-871822.html
|access-date=20 August 2008
|title=Was Ahmed Yildiz the victim of Turkey's first gay honour killing?
|work=Independent
|date=19 July 2008
|first=Nicholas
|last=Birch
| location=London}}</ref> Studies for the years 2007–09 prepared by the German Democratic Turkey Forum show 13 killings in 2007, 5 in 2008 and at least 4 killings in 2009 related to the sexual identity of the victims.<ref>The series can be found under the headline of [http://www.tuerkeiforum.net/enw/index.php/Hate_Crimes_in_Turkey "Hate Crimes in Turkey"]; accessed on 31 March 2011.</ref> On 21 May 2008 the New York-based organization [[Human Rights Watch]] published a report entitled "We Need a Law for Liberation".<ref name=HRW>The report can be accessed at [https://www.hrw.org/en/reports/2008/05/21/we-need-law-liberation-0 this site of HRW]; accessed on 31 March 2011.</ref> The report documents how gay men and transgender people face beatings, robberies, police harassment, and the threat of murder. Human Rights Watch found that, in most cases, the response by the authorities is inadequate if not nonexistent.<ref name=HRW/> In case of hate murders against homosexuals, courts apply the condition of "heavy provocation" and lower sentences.<ref>Report of the Human Rights Observation and Law Commission on LGBTT Individuals within Kaos GL, dated 27 October 2007. A summarized translation was done by the [http://www.tuerkeiforum.net/enw/index.php/Hate_Killings DTF on this site]; accessed on 31 March 2011</ref>

According to the research of [[KAOS GL]], 27% of LGBTQ people who did not hide their sexual identity were discriminated against in the recruitment process in 2017, 8% in 2018, 11% in 2019. The study stated that LGBTQ people, who think that the institutions they apply for are biased, are more inclined to hide their sexual identity, so this rate will be higher if the applicants open to employers.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=TÜRKİYE'DE CİNSEL YÖNELİM VEYA CİNSİYET KİMLİĞİ TEMELİNDE AYRIMCILIĞIN İZLENMESİ RAPORU|url=https://insanhaklarimerkezi.bilgi.edu.tr/media/uploads/2015/02/24/Cinsel_Yonelim_veya_Cinsiyet_Kimligi_Izleme_Raporu.pdf|access-date=|website=}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=İstanbul Valiliği: Onur yürüyüşüne izin verilmeyecek|url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/haberler/2016/06/160617_onur_yuruyusu_valilik|access-date=2020-08-05|website=BBC News Türkçe|date=17 June 2016|language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Onur Yürüyüşü'nde 20 gözaltı|url=https://www.gazeteduvar.com.tr/gundem/2019/06/22/izmirde-onur-yuruyusune-izin-verilmedi/|access-date=2020-08-05|website=www.gazeteduvar.com.tr|date=22 June 2019|language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|date=2017-11-19|title=Ankara Valiliği'nden LGBT etkinliklerine yasak|language=tr|work=BBC News Türkçe|url=https://www.bbc.com/turkce/haberler-turkiye-42043386|access-date=2020-08-05}}</ref>

==LGBTQ civil rights organisations==

[[File:20mayıs Gay pride Ankara Square 12.jpg|220px|thumb|[[Walking against Homophobia and Transphobia|Ankara Pride]] parade in 2012, [[Kızılay, Ankara|Kızılay]], Ankara]]
The EU says that [[Civil society organization|civil society organisations]] are administratively harassed and prosecuted.<ref name=":15" />{{Reference page|page=20}} The major LGBTQ community-based civil rights organisation is [[KAOS GL]], established in 1994 in Ankara by students including [[Yasemin Öz]].<ref name="Öz">{{cite news |last1=Tunali |first1=Tan |title=Defending Human Rights in Turkey: Yasemin Öz |url=https://www.nhc.nl/defending-human-rights-in-turkey-yasemin-oz/ |access-date=7 August 2020 |work=Netherlands Helsinki Committee |date=30 June 2020}}</ref> [[Lambda Istanbul]], a member of [[ILGA-Europe]], established in 1993 in Istanbul, was sued on the charges of acting against [[public morality]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Çakır|first=Bawer|date=29 October 2009|title="Public Morality" Disturbed by LTGB organization...|work=bianet|url=http://bianet.org/english/minorities/117799-public-morality-disturbed-by-ltgb-organization|access-date=21 May 2020}}</ref> The prosecution argued that its name and activities were "against the law and morality." That ruling, sharply criticised by [[Human Rights Watch]],<ref name=HRWLambda>[http://hrw.org/english/docs/2008/06/02/turkey18990.htm Turkey: Court Shows Bias, Dissolves Lambda Istanbul] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113180529/http://hrw.org/english/docs/2008/06/02/turkey18990.htm |date=13 November 2008 }}, ''[[Human Rights Watch]]'', 2 June 2008</ref> was finally overturned by the country's Supreme Court of Appeal on 22 January 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/english/domestic/10844193.asp |title=Appeals court says gay rights unit is OK |date=24 January 2009 |publisher=Hurriyet.com.tr |access-date=20 January 2011}}</ref>

In September 2005, the Ankara Governor's Office accused [[KAOS GL]] of "establishing an organisation that is against the laws and principles of morality."<ref name=HRWLambda/> It also attempted in July 2006 to close the human rights group Pink Life LGBT Association (Pembe Hayat), which works with transgender people, claiming to prosecutors that the association opposed "morality and family structure."<ref name=HRWLambda/> Both charges were ultimately dropped.<ref name=HRWLambda/>

In 2008, a court case was launched to close down Lambda Istanbul, and although a lower court initially decided in favour of closing down the association, the decision was overruled by the [[Constitutional Court of Turkey|Turkish Constitutional Court]] and Lambda Istanbul remains open.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lambdaistanbul.org/php/main.php?menuID=5&altMenuID=5&icerikID=6406 |title=Lambdaistanbul Lezbiyen Gey Biseksüel Travesti Transseksüel Dayanışma Derneği |publisher=Lambdaistanbul.org |access-date=20 January 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100129174708/http://www.lambdaistanbul.org/php/main.php?menuID=5&altMenuID=5&icerikID=6406 |archive-date=29 January 2010 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In 2011, advocacy and support group [[SPoD]] was established. In 2018, the 6th [[İzmir Pride]] was held in [[Alsancak]]. Around 50,000 of LGBTQ members, allies, and human rights supporters participated at the Pride, walking along the waterfront street, [[Kordon, İzmir|Kordon]]. It started on Kıbrıs Şehitleri Avune and it ended in front of [[Türkan Saylan Cultural Center]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bianet.org/english/lgbti/198048-6th-izmir-pride-parade-we-ll-walk-up-to-fear |title=6th İzmir Pride Parade: 'We'll Walk Up to Fear'|publisher= bianet.org |access-date=12 June 2018}}</ref>

In April 2019, Ankara court lifted a ban on [[LGBTQ]] events in Turkey's capital.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hrw.org/news/2019/04/25/turkey-ankara-wakes-court-lifting-lgbti-events-ban |title=In Turkey, Ankara Wakes Up to Court Lifting LGBTI Events Ban |access-date=25 April 2019 |publisher= Human Rights Watch|date=25 April 2019 }}</ref> It is reported that it was Turkish LGBT+ rights group KAOS GL who managed to get it appealed after being unsuccessful the previous year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pinknews.co.uk/2019/04/20/court-lifts-ban-on-lgbt-pride-events-in-ankara-turkey/ |title=Court lifts ban on LGBT Pride events in Turkey's capital city |access-date=20 April 2019 |publisher= Pink News|date=20 April 2019 }}</ref>

In September 2022, thousands of anti-LGBTQ demonstrators marched in Istanbul, demanding the censoring of LGBTQ organizations and the banning of their activities.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-09-18 |title=Thousands march in Turkey to demand ban on LGBTQ groups |url=https://apnews.com/article/middle-east-turkey-gay-rights-istanbul-b06a40c70ae701eab6ce9912e0b632dc |access-date=2022-09-26 |website=AP NEWS |language=en}}</ref> In 2026, LGBTQ rights activist [[Defne Güzel]] was charged with "violating public morality" after her organisation, 17 Mayıs Derneği, published documents about [[Intersex|intersex people]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |date=26 February 2026|title=Judicial harassment of LGBTQI+ rights defender Defne Güzel|url=https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/judicial-harassment-lgbtqi-rights-defender-defne-guzel|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260228105209/https://www.frontlinedefenders.org/en/case/judicial-harassment-lgbtqi-rights-defender-defne-guzel|archive-date=28 February 2026|access-date=28 February 2026|work=[[Front Line Defenders]]|language=en}}</ref>

===Istanbul Pride===
{{Main|Istanbul Pride}}

[[File:Istanbul LGBT Protest.jpg|220px|thumb|Gay Turks and human rights activists chanting slogans against{{citation needed|date=September 2019}} the Turkish government's policies on [[İstiklal Avenue]] in [[Istanbul]]]]
[[File:Gaypride Istanbul 2012.jpg|220px|thumb|[[Istanbul Pride]] parade in 2012]]

[[Istanbul Pride]] is a gay [[pride march]] and [[LGBTQ]] demonstration held annually in [[Turkey]]'s biggest city, [[Istanbul]]. The event first took place in 2003 and now occurs each year on either the last Sunday of June or the first Sunday of July, to mark the end of Istanbul pride week. About 30 people took part in the first Gay Pride Istanbul. The numbers have increased exponentially each year, reaching roughly 5,000 people by 2010. The 2011 gathering attracted over 10,000 people, therefore making Gay Pride Istanbul the biggest march of its kind in the Muslim World.<ref name="kaos">{{cite web | url=http://www.kaosgl.com/sayfa.php?id=9064 | title=19. LGBTT Onur Haftası, Onur Yürüyüşü ile Sona Erdi | publisher=KAOS GL | date=27 June 2011 | access-date=29 June 2011 | last=Tahaoğlu | first=Çicek | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701181746/http://www.kaosgl.com/sayfa.php?id=9064 | archive-date=1 July 2011 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kaosgl.com/sayfa.php?id=9062 | title=Stonewall'dan Bugüne | publisher=KAOS GL | date=24 June 2011 | access-date=29 June 2011 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701182430/http://www.kaosgl.com/sayfa.php?id=9062 | archive-date=1 July 2011 | url-status=dead | df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/n.php?n=homosexuals-demand-rights-at-istanbul8217s-gay-pride-march-2011-06-27 | title=Homosexuals demand rights at Istanbul's Gay Pride March | publisher=Hürriyet Daily News | date=27 June 2011 | access-date=29 June 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntvmsnbc.com/id/25227029/ |title=İstiklal Caddesi 10 bin renk! - Genel |publisher=ntvmsnbc.com |date= |access-date=2012-09-26}}</ref>

Participants assemble in [[Taksim Square]] before marching the entire length of [[İstiklal Avenue]]. This is a wide pedestrian boulevard and one of Istanbul's most important public spaces, the frequent home of [[Bayram (Turkey)|bayram]] and regional festivals.

On 30 June 2013, the pride parade attracted almost 100,000 people.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.telegraaf.nl/tv/21696299/__Gay_Pride_in_Istanbul_groot_succes__.html |title=Gay Pride in Istanbul groot succes - TV &#124; Altijd op de hoogte van het laatste nieuws met Telegraaf.nl [tv&#93; |publisher=Telegraaf.nl |access-date=2013-11-02 |archive-date=28 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170728210152/http://www.telegraaf.nl/tv/21696299/__Gay_Pride_in_Istanbul_groot_succes__.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The protesters were joined by [[2013–14 protests in Turkey|Gezi Park protesters]], making the 2013 Istanbul Pride the biggest pride ever held in Turkey.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dunya.milliyet.com.tr/taksim-deki-onur-yuruyusu-ne-bbc/dunya/detay/1730407/default.htm |title=Taksim'deki Onur Yürüyüşü'ne BBC yorumu: Bugüne kadar... - Milliyet Haber |publisher=Dunya.milliyet.com.tr |access-date=2013-11-02 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104131320/http://dunya.milliyet.com.tr/taksim-deki-onur-yuruyusu-ne-bbc/dunya/detay/1730407/default.htm |archive-date=4 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The 2014 pride attracted more than 100,000 people.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.popkedi.com/yosun-pare/100000-kisi-dile-kolay|title=100.000 KİŞİ! DİLE KOLAY!|work=POPKEDİ|access-date=11 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030752/http://www.popkedi.com/yosun-pare/100000-kisi-dile-kolay|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> The [[European Union]] praised Turkey that the parade went ahead without disruption.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ec.europa.eu/enlargement/pdf/key_documents/2013/package/brochures/turkey_2013.pdf |title=Turkey 2013 |access-date=2013-12-05 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131115052535/http://ec.europa.eu/enlargement/pdf/key_documents/2013/package/brochures/turkey_2013.pdf |archive-date=2013-11-15 }}</ref> On Sunday 29 June 2015, [[Reuters]] reported that Turkish police used a water cannon to disperse the gay pride parade.<ref name="WC"/>

In 2016, the pride march was banned by the local government "for the safety of our citizens, first and foremost the participants’, and for public order.".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://istanbul.gov.tr/tr/guncel/haberler/basin-duyurusu-17062016|title=T.C. İstanbul Valiliği - BASIN DUYURUSU<!-- Bot generated title -->|website=istanbul.gov.tr|access-date=11 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181214055900/http://istanbul.gov.tr/tr/guncel/haberler/basin-duyurusu-17062016|archive-date=14 December 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> LGBTQ organizations have also not been allowed to make a press statement. The governorate of Istanbul once again claimed that a gathering of LGBTQ would not be allowed. "Within Law No: 5442, this request has not been approved due to the terror attacks that have taken place in our country and the area; because provocative acts and events may take place when the sensitivities that have emerged in society are taken into account; and because it may cause a disruption in public order and the people's- including the participants of the event- tranquility, security, and welfare."<ref name=autogenerated1>{{cite web|url=http://kaosgl.org/sayfa.php?id=21952|title=LGBTİ+ Onur Haftası basın açıklamasına da Valilik'ten hassasiyet' yasağı! &#124; Kaos GL Haber Portalı|website=kaosgl.org}}</ref>

In 2017 the [[Governor of İstanbul|Istanbul Governor's Office]] yet again banned the LGBTQ Pride Parade, citing security concerns and public order.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/governors-office-bans-lgbt-pride-march-in-istanbul.aspx?pageID=238&nID=114708&NewsCatID=339|title=Governor's Office bans LGBT Pride March in Istanbul|publisher=hurriyet}}</ref>

In 2018, for the fourth consecutive year the Istanbul Governor's Office yet again banned the LGBTQ Pride Parade, citing security concerns and public order, but around 1,000 people defied the ban, they were met with tear gas and rubber bullets. 11 participants were arrested.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/istanbul-pride-eleven-arrests-official-ban-march-parade-turkey-lgbt-a8426656.html|title=Eleven arrested at Istanbul Pride as march goes ahead despite official ban|date=2 July 2018|website=The Independent}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2018/07/02/europe/istanbul-pride-parade-intl/index.html|title=Istanbul pride: Hundreds of LGBTI+ campaigners defy ban|author=Sheena McKenzie|website=CNN}}</ref>

In 2019, for the fifth consecutive year the Istanbul Governor's Office yet again banned the LGBTQ Pride Parade, citing security concerns and public order.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ahvalnews.com/pride-march/authorities-block-pride-march-second-istanbul-location|title=Authorities block Pride March in second Istanbul location|website=Ahval|language=en|access-date=2019-06-28|archive-date=12 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912115725/https://ahvalnews.com/pride-march/authorities-block-pride-march-second-istanbul-location|url-status=dead}}</ref> subsequently, opposition [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey|Member of the Grand National Assembly]] [[Sezgin Tanrıkulu]] of the [[Republican People's Party]] (CHP) lodged a parliamentary question to the [[Vice President of Turkey]] [[Fuat Oktay]] asking why the deputy governor of Istanbul had banned Istanbul Pride. He also asked how many LGBTQ members had been killed in the last 17 years, the time the ruling party [[Justice and Development Party (Turkey)|Justice and Development Party]] (AKP) ruled the city, due to provocative hate speech, and raised concerns over discrimination against the LGBTQ community.<ref name="m.bianet.org"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://stockholmcf.org/turkish-opposition-deputy-questions-govt-over-banning-pride-marches/|title=Turkish opposition deputy questions gov't over banning pride marches|last=SCF|date=2019-06-25|website=Stockholm Center for Freedom|language=en-US|access-date=2019-06-28}}</ref> On 29 June, hundreds of people defied the ban, they were met with tear gas, shields, pepper gas and plastic bullets from the Police.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bianet.org/haber/police-attack-with-shields-pepper-gas-after-pride-parade-statement-read-209921|title=Police Attack with Shields, Pepper Gas After Pride Parade Statement Read|website=bianet.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://time.com/5617924/istanbul-police-turkey-lgbt-pride-tear-gas/|title=&#124; Time|access-date=14 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702235421/https://time.com/5617924/istanbul-police-turkey-lgbt-pride-tear-gas/|archive-date=2 July 2019|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dw.com/en/istanbul-police-use-tear-gas-to-disperse-gay-pride-march/a-49421078|title=Istanbul police use tear gas to disperse gay pride march &#124; DW &#124; 30.06.2019|website=DW.COM}}</ref>

In June 2022, a small pride march was organized in Istanbul despite the ban. More than 360 people were subsequently arrested, according to the event's organizers.<ref>{{Cite news |agency=Associated Press |date=2022-06-27 |title=More than 300 LGBTQ activists in Istanbul are released after being detained |language=en |work=NPR |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/06/27/1107752526/more-than-300-lgbtq-activists-in-istanbul-are-released-after-being-detained |access-date=2022-09-26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-06-27 |title=Turkey: More than 200 arrests in Istanbul as LGBTQ marchers try to defy Pride ban |language=en |work=Le Monde.fr |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2022/06/27/turkey-more-than-200-arrests-in-istanbul-as-lgbtq-marchers-try-to-defy-pride-ban_5988062_4.html |access-date=2022-09-26}}</ref>

===March against Homophobia and Transphobia===
{{Excerpt|KAOS_GL#March_against_Homophobia_and_Transphobia}}

===University Organizations=== 
The Lesbian and Gay Inter-University Organization ({{langx|tr|Üniversitelerarası Lezbiyen ve Gey Topluluğu - '''LEGATO'''}}) was an [[LGBT]] organization in [[Turkey]] aimed at university students.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LeGaTo {{!}} Üniversiteler Arası Lezbiyen & Gay Topluluğu |url=http://www.unilegato.org/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070107232901/http://www.unilegato.org/ |archive-date=2007-01-07 |access-date=2026-09-14 |website=www.unilegato.org |language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Görkemli |first=Serkan |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/jj.18253820 |title=Grassroots Literacies: Lesbian and Gay Activism and the Internet in Turkey |date=2014 |publisher=State University of New York Press |isbn=978-1-4384-5183-1}}</ref> The idea of bringing together [[homosexual]] university students began in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web |title=To Love Is To Be Organized! Think About It, Rectors! – Civic Space Studies Association |url=https://civicspacestudies.org/2020/07/06/to-love-is-to-be-organized-think-about-it-rectors/ |access-date=2026-09-14 |language=tr-TR}}</ref> By 2014 there were 5 groups: Bilgi Rainbow at [[Istanbul Bilgi University|Bilgi University]], Bilkent Renkli Düşün at [[Bilkent University]], Lion Queer at [[Galatasaray University]], and the Queer Studies Society at [[Hacettepe University]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-11-20 |title=Çukurova Üniversitesi’nin LGBT topluluğu “Gökkuşağı” resmen kuruldu {{!}} STGM |url=https://www.stgm.org.tr/cukurova-universitesinin-lgbt-toplulugu-gokkusagi-resmen-kuruldu |access-date=2026-09-19 |website=www.stgm.org.tr |language=tr |quote=Gökkuşağı Kulübü Türkiye’deki 5. resmî LGBT topluluğu olarak tanındı. Bilgi Üniversitesi’nde Bilgi Rainbow, Bilkent Üniversitesi’nde Bilkent Renkli Düşün’ün dışında Galatasaray Üniversitesi’nde Lion Queer ve Hacettepe Üniversitesi'nde Kuir Araştırmaları Topluluğu adlı LGBT toplulukları bulunuyor. |trans-quote=The Rainbow Club has been recognized as the fifth official LGBT student group in Turkey. In addition to Bilgi Rainbow at Bilgi University and Bilkent Renkli Düşün at Bilkent University, there are LGBT groups known as Lion Queer at Galatasaray University and the Queer Studies Society at Hacettepe University.}}</ref>

|[[Conversion therapy]] banned

However, certified mental health professionals (psychiatrists and psychologists) are ethically and professionally prohibited from conducting conversion therapy by major national bodies like the Psychiatric Association of Turkey. Despite this, unlicensed or underground religious organizations are reported to perform these practices clandestinely<ref>{{cite web |title=Homofobik ve Transfobik Kitap ve Uygulamalar Hakkında
